entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Finan of Lindisfarne, also known as Saint Finan, was an Irish monk trained at Iona Abbey in Scotland who became the second bishop of Lindisfarne from 651 until 661. Born in Ireland in the late 6th century, Finan was ordained as a monk and later became a prominent figure in the Lindisfarne community. He played a crucial role in the establishment of the Lindisfarne monastery, which became a center of learning and spirituality for the Celtic Christian community. Finan's leadership and teachings helped shape the religious and cultural identity of the Lindisfarne monks, who developed a unique blend of Celtic and Christian traditions. His legacy extended beyond his own community, influencing the development of early Christianity in the British Isles and the transmission of Celtic Christian texts and art. Finan of Lindisfarne was revered as a saint, and his feast day is celebrated on June 25th. His contributions to the history of early Christianity and the preservation of Celtic Christian traditions have left a lasting impact on the cultural heritage of the British Isles.
